title: Why do we say went and not goed?
examples: Why is the past of go went?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Add ed, or a whole new word?

explain.say: Here is something funny. Little children everywhere say things like I goed to the park. That is not silly at all: it shows they have learned the rule! Look at the left of the board: play, played; jump, jumped. Just add ed.

draw.text: Why do we say went and not goed?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Add ed, or a whole new word?

explain.say: Verbs that follow the add ed rule are called regular verbs. Most English verbs are regular. Can you make the past of paint? Painted! See how easy?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Add ed, or a whole new word?

explain.say: But look at the other group on the board: go, went; eat, ate; see, saw. These verbs change in their own way. They are called irregular verbs, which means they break the rule. Which one surprises you most?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Add ed, or a whole new word?

explain.say: Why is went so strange? Look at the board. Went is four sounds: w, e, n, t. It used to be the past of another verb, wend, which means to travel. Long ago, English swapped it in for the past of go!

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Went once belonged to the verb wend

explain.say: Great work! The irregular verbs are the ones we use most, like go, be, have and eat. Using them so much kept their old shapes alive. Look back at the irregular group. Challenge: what is the past of swim, sing and drink?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Add ed, or a whole new word?

faq.a: An irregular verb does not add ed in the past. It changes in its own way: go becomes went, eat becomes ate, and see becomes saw.
A regular verb makes its past by adding ed: play, played; cook, cooked. Most English verbs are regular.
No, the past of go is went. But young children say goed because they have learned the add ed rule, which is a clever step in learning to talk.

faq.q: Why is the past of go went?
faq.a: Went was first the past of an old verb, wend, meaning to travel. About 500 years ago English started using went as the past of go instead.

faq.q: How do I learn irregular verbs?
faq.a: Learn them in little sets that sound alike: sing, sang, sung; ring, rang, rung; drink, drank, drunk. Saying them aloud helps them stick.

facts: Went was originally the past tense of the verb wend, meaning to go or travel.
The most common English verbs, like be, have, go and say, are mostly irregular.
